pathogen.value: Avian infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a coronavirus with many strains

value: in layers: dropped egg production, misshapen or discolored eggs, thin or watery-white eggs

mortality.value: Nearly all unvaccinated birds get sick; deaths can reach up to 60% in unvaccinated flocks depending on the virus strain, and some strains cause kidney failure deaths in young birds

diagnosis.value: Hard to tell apart from other chicken respiratory illnesses by signs alone; confirming it needs isolating and characterizing the virus, usually by PCR-based genetic testing, or detecting antibodies

value: vaccination, though many strains and vaccine failures make full protection difficult

treatment_overview.value: No specific treatment; antibiotics may be given to prevent secondary infections

summary.value: Avian infectious bronchitis is a fast-spreading viral respiratory illness of chickens that also drops egg production and quality in laying hens. There is no cure, so prevention relies on vaccination and good biosecurity, though the virus has many strains that can get around existing vaccines.
